review_notes:
I read all of BurgersJets.lean. I also read the JetExpr definitions in Equations/JetAlgebra.lean: eval, D, σx, σh, logGradientJet, eval_σx, eval_σh and hasDerivAt_eval. I grepped for uses of burgers0–3 and scaledHeatJet_time0–3 in HeatTransform.lean and BackwardPolynomials.lean.

The file declares no simp attributes or simp sets, and I found no unwanted expansion, rewrite cycle or competing rules.

- scaledHeatJet_expr is deliberately not @[simp]. It rewrites a plain definition into a larger JetExpr.eval expression and needs hypotheses hψ and hc. It is only applied locally through simp_rw and simpa only.
- The burgers0–3 lemmas are specific closed-form instances. Their statements contain eval R (logGradientJet k) on the right-hand side, so they would not be sensible simp lemmas. They are applied by explicit rw.
- eval_σx and eval_σh in JetAlgebra.lean are not @[simp]. They are used through simp only in only three places, so marking them @[simp] would help little. The rubric advises against adding simp attributes only because an identity looks simple.
- The burgers proofs use `simp only [logGradientJet,D,σh,σx,eval]; norm_num; ring`. That is a robustness or style concern, not a defect in the simp interface.

I could not run Lean, so I did not check whether `norm_num` after `simp only` is fragile.
